meta.subtitle: AI weapons-screening subscription vendor whose growth is priced at today's sales multiple, with control and investigation overhangs still open

analystCommentary: Evolv Technologies sells AI-powered weapons screening as a Security-as-a-Service subscription, and the June quarter showed the top line still compounding: Q2'26 revenue was $43.8M, up 34.4% year over year. The quality of the improvement below the top line is less clear. The trailing net loss is far smaller than the trailing operating loss, the pack does not itemize the difference, and Q2'26's operating margin was weaker than the trailing figure. Consensus still models losses through FY27. Management has also disclosed material weaknesses in internal control that contributed to a restatement of the 2022 and 2023 annual periods and two 2024 quarters, and an ad hoc board committee opened an investigation into sales practices in September 2024 whose outcome the pack does not report. The shares, at $4.91, sit near the bottom of their $4.79 to $8.81 52-week range, and no source in the pack explains the decline. We rate Evolv HOLD with a $4.50 to $6.50 range. Today's price-to-sales multiple applied to consensus FY26 revenue gives a Base only a little above the current price, and that modest expected return does not compensate for a Bear we price as a real de-rating of the recurring revenue base.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Evolv Technologies Holdings, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, develops and sells AI-powered security screening products in the United States and internationally. Its platform centers on two hardware products: Evolv Express, designed to screen high volumes of people for concealed threats such as firearms and large tactical knives, and Evolv eXpedite, an autonomous AI-based system for screening bags without a trained X-ray operator. Both operate only with Evolv's proprietary software and cloud services, and the subscription bundles Evolv Insights, a cloud analytics application that reports throughput volumes, alarm statistics and system performance, together with onsite support and repair for the full term. Customers span education, healthcare, professional sports, live entertainment, tourist attractions, houses of worship and industrial workplaces, and adoption to date has been primarily within the United States.

thesis.body: The case for owning Evolv is a hardware-enabled subscription platform growing quickly: revenue rose 40.5% in FY25 to $145.9M, gross margin was 51.6% in FY25 after a 57.2% peak in FY24, and operating cash flow turned non-negative in FY25 on the vendor's rounding. The case against is that operating losses persist, consensus EPS stays negative through FY27, the reported figures carry a restatement history, and the sales-practices investigation has no reported outcome. At $4.91 the market already prices much of that skepticism. Holding today's 5.2x price-to-sales on consensus FY26 revenue puts our Base only a little above the price, so the shares look roughly fairly valued rather than cheap. The upside case needs evidence on operating profit and on controls that the pack does not yet show.

catalysts: A conclusion of the September 2024 sales-practices investigation and remediation of the material weaknesses, which would ease the main overhang on the multiple.
Second-half revenue delivery against the FY26 consensus.
An operating margin that resumes improving after the Q2'26 step back.
Disclosure of Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation, the indicators management highlights but this pack does not quantify.
Purchase-subscription product revenue replacing the expired Columbia Tech license revenue.
risks: Material weaknesses in internal control contributed to a restatement of the 2022 and 2023 annual periods and two 2024 quarters.
The ad hoc board committee's investigation into sales practices, opened in September 2024, has no reported outcome in the pack.
Consensus models losses through FY27, and the 10-K says the company may require additional capital.
Customers may not renew their typical four-year subscriptions, or may renew at lower revenue.
Loss of the Evolv Express SAFETY Act designation could carry reputational and financial consequences.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue has compounded off a small base: FY22 grew 125.4%, FY23 50.9%, FY24 30.5% and FY25 40.5% to $145.9M. Growth held up in 2026. Q2'26 revenue of $43.8M was {+ up 34.4% +} year over year, and revenue for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $90.1 million against $64.6 million a year earlier. Gross margin recovered from 2.7% in FY22 to 40.1% in FY23 and peaked at 57.2% in FY24 before easing to 51.6% in FY25; the trailing-twelve-month figure is 49.9%, so the margin has not regained its FY24 level. The operating line has improved over the years but not steadily in 2026: operating margin moved from -79.2% in FY24 to -33.2% in FY25 and -20.8% over the trailing twelve months, yet Q2'26 came in at {- -24.1% -}, weaker than the trailing figure. The net line looks much better than the operating line. The six-month net loss narrowed to $14.3 million from $42.2 million, and the trailing net margin is -3.0% against the trailing operating margin above, so items below operating income offset most of the operating loss. The pack does not itemize those items. The 10-K warns that changes in the value of warrants, earn-out shares and founder shares carried as liabilities could have a material effect on financial results, but we cannot tell from the pack whether they explain the gap, so we judge progress on the operating margin rather than the net loss. FY25 net income was -$33.1M and diluted EPS -$0.20, better than -$0.34 in FY24. Consensus expects FY26 revenue of about $182.4M, up 25%, and $218.9M in FY27, with EPS of -$0.08 and -$0.04, so the Street models no profitable year in its forecast window.
financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet holds more cash than debt, but not by much. FY25 total debt was $28.6M and net debt was -$20.6M, so cash and short-term investments exceeded borrowings at year-end. Liquidity has thinned steadily: the current ratio fell from 13.61 in FY21 to 1.26 in FY24 and 1.23 in FY25, and is 1.18 on a trailing basis. Total equity was about $0.1B at FY25 on the vendor's rounding. The 10-K adds two constraints. The company's debt instrument carries affirmative and negative covenants, including financial covenants, that may limit operating flexibility, and the company may require additional capital to support growth, which might not be available. The balance sheet is not stretched today, but with a modest net cash cushion and losses still modeled it leaves little room to absorb a setback without outside funding.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow was negative from FY21 through FY24 and turned non-negative in FY25: the vendor's $B table shows it without the minus sign of the two prior years, though the table's rounding hides its size. The pack carries no capital expenditure or free cash flow after FY21, so we cannot say whether operations covered investment spending. The dividend yield is 0.00% and no repurchases are recorded. Two trailing-twelve-month credit measures need care. Interest coverage is -9.7x because operating earnings are negative. Net debt to EBITDA prints as a positive multiple, but net debt and EBITDA are both negative, so the ratio does not measure leverage and we do not use it; the net cash position in the balance sheet section is the better read. Whether operating cash flow stays non-negative through 2026 matters more to this stock than any ratio, because it decides whether the company needs outside capital.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Earnings multiples carry no signal while Evolv loses money: P/E is -245.5x, EV/EBITDA -98.8x and the vendor's NTM forward P/E -64.0x, and the FY27 forward P/E is not meaningful because consensus expects a loss. Price-to-sales of 5.2x is the usable anchor. The page does not label the revenue window behind it, so we apply it to consensus revenue and do not treat it as a trailing figure. The pack has no peer column, so we cannot say whether that multiple is high or low against comparable companies, and we argue the multiple from Evolv's own growth, margins and risks. The Street is uniformly positive: five analysts rate the stock Buy, the consensus target is $9.85, the median $10.00 and the range $8.00 to $11.25, so even the lowest target sits well above the price. We use that lowest target as our Bull rather than our Base, because reaching it needs a re-rating that consensus EPS, negative through FY27, does not yet support.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: FY27 revenue reaches the consensus $218.9M, the operating margin resumes improving after Q2'26, and the investigation and control weaknesses are put behind the company; the shares re-rate to the lowest Street target of $8.00, which needs a sales multiple above today's even on FY27E revenue, and which sits below the $8.81 the shares reached within the past year.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue reaches the FY26E consensus of $182.4M and losses persist as modeled; the shares hold today's 5.2x price-to-sales, which on $182.4M of revenue and the 179.87M shares behind the market cap gives $5.27. Slowing growth and a Q2'26 operating margin weaker than the trailing figure argue for a lower multiple, while first-half revenue covering about half of FY26E and a trailing operating margin well ahead of FY25's argue for a higher one, so we hold it.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The investigation, a control lapse or a renewal shortfall puts the recurring base in question. FY26E consensus revenue is still delivered, but the market pays three times sales, a little over half today's multiple and our assumption for revenue whose durability is in doubt; on the same revenue and share count as the Base that gives $3.04, well below the $4.79 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight the Base at 50% and the Bull and Bear at 25% each. The Base is the most likely outcome because FY26 revenue looks reachable on first-half results and the pack shows nothing that would change how the market prices this revenue over the next year. The Bull and Bear carry equal weight because the near-term evidence cuts both ways. Revenue growth and operating cash flow that turned non-negative in FY25 support the Bull. The Bear rests on an investigation with no reported outcome, control weaknesses with no reported remediation and the 10-K's warning that more capital may be needed; any one of these coming to a head is the event the Bear prices.

On these weights the expected upside is +9.9%, the bear-case downside -38.1% and reward/risk 0.26×. The scenarios derive HOLD, and HOLD is our call. Reward/risk decides it rather than expected upside: that ratio sits far below the 0.50× the BUY test needs, so a slightly higher expected upside would not change the label.

The call turns on two judgments, and we tested each in both directions. A Bear at four times sales instead of three, our assumption for a de-rating that stops short of doubting the recurring base, would derive BUY, while a deeper Bear would leave HOLD in place. A Base a full turn above today's multiple would also derive BUY, while a turn below would leave the expected upside near zero, still HOLD. We price the Bear at the deeper multiple because the risks behind it go to the reliability of the revenue itself, not only to its growth rate. We hold the Base multiple because the pack gives no evidence the market will pay more for this revenue a year out while operating losses persist. Our $4.50 to $6.50 range brackets the Base: the low end sits just below the 52-week low, and the high end allows roughly for today's multiple holding on FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Evolv reports one consolidated segment; FY25 revenue of $145.9M is shown entirely as a single Security-as-a-Service line, and the vendor breaks out no product or geographic mix. The offering bundles hardware, proprietary software, cloud connectivity and onsite support and repair for the full multi-year term. It is sold through two models: a pure subscription, where the customer leases the hardware, and a purchase subscription, where the customer buys the hardware outright; each requires an active, connected software subscription. The 10-K says a substantial portion of revenue is recognized ratably over the term of customer agreements, so changes in sales show up in reported results only gradually.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: Each deployment pairs Evolv-only hardware with a proprietary, connected software subscription and onsite support, and the 10-K describes typical four-year subscriptions. The hardware and software are designed to operate together and not as standalone offerings, which raises the cost of leaving the platform mid-term.

moatFactors.name: Data and AI feedback loop
moatFactors.body: A large and growing installed base generates anonymized screening data that the company uses to train and update its detection models, which customers receive through software updates. A larger base feeds more real-world data into model improvement, a loop a new entrant would take time to build.

moatFactors.name: Recurring revenue
moatFactors.body: The Security-as-a-Service model produces subscription revenue over multi-year contracts, and management points to Annual Recurring Revenue and Remaining Performance Obligation as measures of its durability. Neither is quantified in this pack, so the strength of this factor rests on the model's design rather than on disclosed figures.

moatFactors.name: Regulatory designation
moatFactors.body: Evolv Express carries a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology designation under the Homeland Security SAFETY Act, a credential a competitor would need to obtain; the 10-K lists the loss of that designation as a risk, so the advantage is real but not guaranteed.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. The switching costs, the data loop and the SAFETY Act designation are real, but the company describes the AI-based weapons-detection market as new and evolving, one that may grow more slowly or differently than it expects, and it competes with new entrants and other potential competitors. Evolv has never been profitable, so it has not yet shown that the installed base converts into sustained earnings. Renewals of multi-year contracts are the test of whether the switching costs hold; until renewal outcomes are disclosed, a narrow rating is the most the evidence supports.

points: First-half revenue already covers about half of the FY26E consensus revenue of $182.4M: six-month revenue was $90.1 million, so the full-year figure needs a second half only slightly larger than the January-to-June period. That implies a much slower year-over-year pace in the second half than the 34.4% of Q2'26. The sources give no reason for such a slowdown, so the consensus looks reachable, and the open question is the pace after FY26.
Consensus has FY27 revenue at $218.9M, so the Street expects growth to continue but at a slower rate than the 25% it models for FY26.

The Columbia Tech distributor-licensing agreement expired on December 31, 2025, and that demand now runs through the purchase subscription model; management says license revenue has reduced to zero and is replaced by increased product revenue, which provides an increase in gross profit over the term of the related subscription contract.

Adoption has been primarily in the United States, and management expects increased adoption in foreign markets in the near future as it explores expansion; the 10-K also lists international expansion as a source of operational, regulatory and compliance risk.

The November 5, 2025 non-exclusive contract manufacturing agreement with Plexus is meant to add scalability and geographic diversification; management says it keeps sufficient inventory and committed production capacity with its existing contract manufacturer while Plexus is brought on.

management.leadership: The pack carries no earnings-call transcript, and the proxy excerpt lists names without titles, so we do not assign roles to individuals. We judge management through what it has disclosed and done. In September 2024 an ad hoc committee of independent directors opened an investigation into the company's sales practices, and the 10-K reports material weaknesses in internal control that contributed to a restatement; the pack reports neither an outcome for the investigation nor completed remediation. On operations, management ended the Columbia Tech licensing model and added Plexus as a second contract manufacturer, both consistent with its stated aims of better margins and supply-chain resilience. Execution on growth looks credible, but the reliability of reporting is not yet restored, and that, more than strategy, limits what we are willing to pay for the shares.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital goes entirely back into the business: the dividend yield is 0.00% and the pack records no share repurchases. With a modest net cash position and the 10-K's statement that the company may require additional capital, the question for holders is funding rather than returns; if operating cash flow turned negative again, the 10-K warns that additional capital might not be available, and the pack does not say whether it would come from debt or equity; any equity raise would dilute existing holders. Management's clearest allocation choice in the pack is the move from license fees to purchase subscriptions, which gives up the license fee in exchange for product revenue and subscription gross profit over the contract term. That is a sensible trade for a recurring-revenue model, with the gain arriving, in management's words, over the term of the related subscription contract.
management.governance: Governance rests on the proxy filed April 30, 2026. The board has determined that its non-employee directors are independent under Nasdaq rules, naming Kevin Charlton, Neil Glat, Henrik K hl (appointed February 12, 2026), David Mounts-Gonzales, Rajan Naik, Richard Shapiro, Kimberly Sheehy and Mark Sullivan; Bilal Zuberi resigned on February 10, 2026. All Audit and Compensation Committee members meet the committee independence requirements. In finding Mr. Naik independent, the board considered that he has no direct involvement or material interest in the company's relationship with Motorola Solutions. The board has no standing risk-management committee and oversees risk directly and through its standing committees, with the Audit Committee responsible for risk-assessment policies. The board structure gives outside holders no specific concern; the concern is the control environment, where the material weaknesses and the restatement mean the board's oversight has yet to show results in reported figures.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy reports director and officer holdings as of March 20, 2026, against 179,355,563 Class A shares outstanding. Directors and executive officers as a group held 9,636,602 shares, 5.2% of the class, led by Michael Ellenbogen at 2.5% and Anil Chitkara at 1.8%, with every other listed director and officer below 1%. The 5% holder rows are older than that date. BlackRock's 9,391,975 shares rest on a Schedule 13G filed on November 8, 2024, nearly two years before this 10-Q, so they say little about its holding today. The Vanguard Group's 11,981,998 shares (6.7%) rest on a Schedule 13G/A filed on October 30, 2025; a further 13G/A filed on March 26, 2026 says that after an internal realignment effective January 12, 2026 it no longer beneficially owns the shares directly, with its subsidiaries and divisions reporting separately. For an outside holder, this is a widely held register: no individual, no institution and not even the insider group together can steer a vote, so control is not a concern. Alignment is real but limited, resting on two meaningful insider stakes, while the dated institutional rows show no committed owner pressing on the control remediation; outside holders should not count on one.

idiosyncratic: Internal control and restatement: the 10-K says material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting contributed to the restatement of the annual periods ended December 31, 2022 and 2023, the quarterly periods in those years beginning with the second quarter of 2022, and the periods ended March 31, 2024 and June 30, 2024. Until remediation is shown, every reported figure, including the narrowing loss, carries less weight than it would at a company with a clean history.

Sales-practices investigation: in September 2024 an ad hoc committee of independent directors began investigating the company's sales practices. The pack reports no outcome, so the legal, reputational and financial consequences remain open, and a finding that touched recognized revenue would go to the heart of the subscription case.

Detection performance: the 10-K warns that if its products fail or are perceived to fail to detect threats, the business could be harmed. For a security product sold on detection, a single prominent miss could weigh on renewals and new orders at once.

Subscription renewals: management flags the risk of losing recurring revenue if customers do not renew their typical four-year subscriptions or renew at lower revenue, and of significant losses if returned systems cannot be profitably redeployed.

SAFETY Act designation: loss of the Evolv Express designation as a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology under the Homeland Security SAFETY Act could result in adverse reputational and financial consequences.
risks.systemic: Broader conditions bear on the model. Management expects results to fluctuate with inflation and interest rates on business spending, supply-chain constraints, public-health emergencies, geopolitical conflict and recessionary trends. Component costs, long lead times, supply shortages and tariff volatility could disrupt the supply chain and pressure cost of revenue, including the memory and compute components used in AI-enabled products; the second contract manufacturer addresses capacity but not component prices. A portion of revenue comes from government entities, whose budgets and procurement cycles add sensitivity to the fiscal and political backdrop. As a small, unprofitable company, Evolv's stock has been and may continue to be highly volatile, which the move from the top to the bottom of its 52-week range illustrates.

body: We rate Evolv HOLD with a target range of $4.50 to $6.50. This revision replaces our earlier BUY: that Base did not follow from its own 5.2x multiple, and once the Base and Bear each follow their stated anchors the scenarios derive HOLD. Evolv is a growing subscription business whose revenue for FY26 looks reachable, but at today's multiple that growth is largely in the price, and the overhangs on its reported figures justify a Bear deep enough that the reward does not cover the risk.

Two developments would move us toward BUY: a concluded investigation together with remediation of the control weaknesses, which would narrow the Bear we price, and an operating margin back on an improving path after Q2'26. A capital raise, or second-half revenue short of a FY26 consensus that first-half results make look reachable, would move us toward the Bear. On unchanged scenarios, the page would derive BUY only if the price fell somewhat below the $4.79 52-week low, and would derive SELL at a price not far above our Base.
